rationale: Combined product: the obligation the third confirmed defect left as its remaining discriminator, and the check that resolves it. The obligation c-at-most-one-leader-per-term states Raft's central safety property for this implementation - a term must have at most one leader - and binds the election and authority-acquisition paths together: the vote rule that limits a voter to one vote per term, the vote path that accepts a leadership-transfer stimulus while a leader is known, and the candidate path that persists a self-vote for its proposed term and records itself as the known leader. The check drives that chain end to end with public APIs only: a heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries is held inside a lagging voter's StableStore write, the following election is won with that voter's grant while a third voter abstains, the release drops the lagging voter's published term by one, and the leader's transfer to it makes it propose the term it already voted in and win a quorum from the abstaining voter. The plan states the fixed inputs, the binding, the oracle with the applicability that restricts the comparison to the case the property is about, and the limits.

candidate.rationale: Fourth Candidate, opened from the remaining unknown recorded on the vote-record fact and on the candidate behavior after the local vote-once obligation was confirmed. It states the global safety property that the local rule exists to protect, and binds it to the election, vote and transfer paths whose combination the check exercises.

question.question: Can one election term have two leaders in this implementation, i.e. can a node establish itself as leader for a term while another node already holds the leadership of that same term?
question.importance: At most one leader per term is the property the whole replicated log rests on: a term with two leaders lets two disjoint sets of clients be told they are led in the same term, and each leader can accept and commit entries at the same indexes, so a state machine can diverge on data that was acknowledged to clients. The implementation relies on its own vote rule for this (a voter refuses a second different vote in a term), so any path that lets the same term be voted twice, or that accepts a transfer stimulus while a leader is known, can break it. Two leaders in one term is therefore the strongest consequence reachable inside this library, and the earlier confirmed defects make the enabling conditions concrete.
participants: the voter that abstains from the election
the lagging voter that later becomes the second leader
the transport callback that carries the stale term write
objects: raftState.state and currentTerm on each node
contexts: three voters where one is unreachable for exactly one election and one lags by one published term
the sitting leader transferring leadership to the lagging voter while its published term is still one below the term it voted in
event_paths: connection goroutine: a heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries with the stale term is adopted and its term write is held
main loop: the following election is granted by the lagging voter, which records its vote for the winning candidate; the abstaining voter records nothing
release: the held write publishes the lower term on the lagging voter

transfer: the leader sends TimeoutNow, the target proposes the published term plus one, overwrites its record with a self-vote and is granted by the abstaining voter, reaching a second quorum in the same term

supporting_behavior_ids.b-elect-self: the path that proposes the already-voted term and persists the self-vote that makes the second leadership possible
supporting_behavior_ids.b-heartbeat-fastpath: the entry point that lowers the published term without being serialized with the main goroutine

counterevidence: Two leaders in one term is transient here: each leader reverts to follower when it receives traffic from the other, so the state is observable at the instant it is created rather than lasting.

The verdicts on the vote path are otherwise conservative: a voter that has voted in a term refuses a different candidate, and a leader refuses a transfer request from a candidate whose vote it already recorded.
The chain needs a voter whose record for the term is still empty; if every other voter had already voted, the second quorum would be unreachable.
A reader may consider leadership transfer outside the safety argument because it is an operator action; the library accepts it at any time, including immediately after an election.
unknowns: whether a lasting dual-leader state is reachable, for instance by keeping the two leaders from learning about each other
whether conflicting entries can be committed by the two leaders of one term, which this check does not exercise
whether a caller-visible path in this repository treats the transient overlap as an error
question.trigger_rationale: The vote path accepts a request that carries the leadership-transfer flag even while another leader is known, so a voter's own record is the only barrier against a second quorum in a term that already has a leader; that record is written without consultation by the candidate path, whose proposed term is derived from a published term that the heartbeat callback can lower by one; and a node that already voted in the term can therefore propose it again and keep the vote as its own. The three mechanisms were each confirmed separately, so the remaining question is whether one legal history can chain them into a second leadership of a live term.

obligation.description: A term must have at most one leader: when a node establishes itself as leader for term T - by counting a quorum of grants and recording itself as the known leader - no other node may already hold the leadership of T. The requirement binds the election, vote and authority-acquisition paths together, including the rule that a voter persists at most one vote per term and the path that accepts a leadership-transfer stimulus while another leader is known.

scope.description: A cluster of voters in the captured module, exercising elections, a delayed term write from the heartbeat callback on the transport goroutine, and a leadership transfer initiated through the public API.
assumptions: the transported RPCs may be delayed or lost, and the injected stores may be slow
the leadership-transfer API may be called by the operator at any time
a node that already voted in a term may be asked to vote again after its published term drops
excluded: the local vote-record obligation, which was checked separately and is the enabling mechanism here
the client-visible consequences of two leaders, which this check does not exercise
behaviour of transports outside this module

pending: whether a lasting dual-leader state is reachable
whether conflicting client entries can be committed by two leaders of one term

grounding.derivation: Leadership is established by counting grants from a quorum and recording the node itself as the known leader (s-raft-candidate-vote). The grant path enforces at most one vote per term by comparing the request with the durable record, but it exempts requests that carry the leadership-transfer flag from the known-leader check (s-raft-vote-record, s-raft-request-vote-filter). The candidate path writes a self-vote for its proposed term, which is the published term plus one, without consulting that record (s-raft-elect-self, s-raft-set-current-term), and the published term can be lowered by a delayed write from the heartbeat callback because that entry point is not serialized with the main goroutine (s-raft-process-heartbeat, s-net-fastpath). A history in which a voter's record for term T holds one candidate and, after its published term drops to T-1, a transfer stimulus makes it propose T again therefore produces a second quorum for T while the first leader still holds T.
grounding.applicability: Applies to a voter set in which one voter is unreachable for the election that establishes the first leader and one voter lags by a published term; the check uses a three-voter cluster, a blocked endpoint and a seeded term on injected stores.
unresolved: whether the same chain needs the seeded term values or can be reached by ordinary elections
whether the dual leadership can be made to persist
conflicts: the vote path accepts a leadership-transfer request while another leader is known, leaving each voter's own record as the only barrier to a second quorum in a term that already has a leader
alternatives: if the transfer exemption were restricted to the leadership the sender actually holds, the second quorum would need a different enabling path
if the candidate path consulted the vote record before writing, the second proposal of an already-voted term would be refused locally

associations.rationale: This entry point is where the second leadership of a term is acquired: it proposes a term derived from a value another entry point can lower, writes a self-vote for it without comparing the record, and then counts grants, one of which comes from a voter that abstains from the first election for that term.

bindings.description: Raft.electSelf increments the published current term, persists a self-vote for the new term and then asks the peers for votes. It is the path through which the lagging voter proposes the term it already voted in, overwrites its own record, and collects the second quorum of that term.
pending: whether the intended repair is a guard in this path or a restriction of the transfer exemption in the vote path
